steps.what: Review the referring clinician's question and relevant urology findings
Discuss the urological problem and decide specialist advice
Write the specialist consultation report from actual findings and advice

loop.purpose: Draft consultation wording from urologist-entered findings and advice
loop.input: actual findings and advice entered by the urologist within s3
loop.check: Urologist verifies every clinical claim, laterality, negation, uncertainty, recommendation and attribution against the encounter and source record
loop.stop: Missing source support or two failed drafts means manual report writing in retained time
loop.why_not_simpler: Use native clinical fields first; variable explanation of specialist advice still needs wording and complete clinical meaning review

steps.what: Check final consultation report, patient and authorised recipient
outputs: final checked consultation report and recipient

steps.what: Send the final consultation report to the requesting clinician
inputs: final checked consultation report and recipient

tasks.design: Test native clinical-record category {OTHER} report templates, then draft only explanatory wording from the urologist's entered consultation facts. Keep clinical review, specialist advice and all meaning checks; a separate report send follows checking the completed version and recipient.
tasks.previous_blocker: A consultation report must accurately distinguish findings, uncertainty and recommendations.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded source-limited drafting can shorten initial wording with full specialist review.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous findings and advice outside the requesting clinician's original question.
tasks.human_edge: Make and explain an accountable specialist judgement.
tasks.altitude: Some report wording is shorter; specialist responsibility remains.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber supports consultation-note drafting with clinician validation; this does not establish autonomous specialist advice or a local saving.

assumptions: Boundary models a consultation with an actual report sent to an authorised requesting clinician outside the organisation; internal-only consultation uses internal authority for the send. Shares are provisional.

The referring clinician supplies the question and source record; the urologist checks it in s1 and develops advice in s2. s3 counts original fact entry, wording, meaning review and repair. No free recording, transcript or structured decision feed is assumed.

{OTHER} is the clinical record and secure clinical-message module. Native fields first; only initial wording, 10% of s3, is removed. Ordinary author saves stay fully retained and ungated. This report is advice, not an automatic prescription or treatment-order activation.

s4 checks the final completed report, patient and exact authorised recipient before s5; edits void approval. Any separate medication or procedure order requires its own final-version authorisation and release.
research_questions: Does drafting preserve laterality, uncertainty and advice attribution without adding review time?

already_counted.description: Source capture, draft review/repair and final report verification remain.

incremental.description: Urologist checks report templates and drafting behaviour after changes.

approvals.approved_version: s4 final consultation report, patient identity and exact authorised requesting clinician destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 30*0.10=3 wording hours removed less 0.8 upkeep gives 2.2 net. Cautious case: conflicting imaging and history require mostly manual explanation, leaving 0.9 hours of straightforward findings wording removed and 0.1 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct nurses, residents and clinical staff in patient care

steps.what: Review current patient status, care plans and staff responsibilities
Direct staff, discuss care priorities and decide necessary patient-care instructions
Enter the actual patient-care instructions in the clinical order draft
Check final care orders, patient, timing and responsible staff
outputs: final checked care orders and responsible staff

steps.what: Activate the checked care orders for the responsible clinical staff
inputs: final checked care orders and responsible staff

tasks.design: Use native patient-context order fields in the clinical-record category {OTHER} to avoid repeated identifier entry. Retain rounds, staff direction, clinical instruction writing and complete checks; activate the exact final orders separately after authorisation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Directions must reflect the current patient and staff capability.
tasks.enabler_now: Native patient-context forms can remove repeated identity entry without proposing care.
tasks.still_hard: Changing clinical priorities and making sure staff understand the instruction.
tasks.human_edge: Lead the team and recognise when a plan needs reconsideration.
tasks.altitude: Very small entry relief; unchanged clinical leadership.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native patient-context order forms can reuse identifiers while clinical care instructions and authorisation remain with the practitioner.

assumptions: Boundary is the urologist's staff-direction cycle including actual care orders. Pure verbal coordination has a different mix; shares are provisional.

The care team supplies current observations and staff allocation; the urologist verifies context in s1 and makes care decisions in s2. s3 captures actual instructions manually. No new structured decision feed or unpriced transcript.

Test native patient context first. Only repeated patient identifier entry, 5% of s3, is removed; clinical fields, corrections and ordinary draft saving stay. s4 checks the completed order, exact patient, timing and responsible staff before s5 formally activates it; edits void approval.
Staff execution labour is outside the focal denominator and earns no saving. No automatic priority, diagnosis or treatment recommendation is proposed.
research_questions: Does native context remove repeated identity entry beyond today's order screen?

already_counted.description: Clinical source review, directions, instruction capture and final order checks remain.

incremental.description: Urologist checks context fields after order-screen changes.

approvals.approved_version: s4 complete final care orders, exact patient, timing and responsible clinical staff; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 20*0.05=1 identifier hour removed less 0.3 upkeep gives 0.7 net. Cautious case: urgent or cross-ward orders require fresh patient-context checks, leaving 0.3 hours of reuse and zero net; all directions and activation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prescribe for erectile dysfunction, infertility or ejaculation problems

steps.what: Assess erectile dysfunction, infertility or ejaculation problems and treatment suitability
Review medication, contraindications, interactions and required dose adjustments
Enter the chosen medication, strength, dose, route and instructions
Check the final prescription, patient, regimen, warnings and pharmacy destination
outputs: final checked prescription and pharmacy destination

steps.what: Authorise and send the checked prescription to the pharmacy
inputs: final checked prescription and pharmacy destination

tasks.design: Test native medication favourites in the clinical prescribing category {OTHER} to reuse standard product, strength and route fields after the urologist selects treatment. Retain patient assessment, surveillance review, individual regimen entry and complete prescription checking; the exact prescription is issued separately after its final check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standard product entry is repetitive, but suitability and dosing remain patient-specific.
tasks.enabler_now: Native prescribing favourites can reduce catalogue selection and fixed-field typing.
tasks.still_hard: Contraindications, interactions, fertility goals and individual treatment risks.
tasks.human_edge: Balance evidence, preferences and clinical risk before prescribing.
tasks.altitude: Less fixed prescription entry; unchanged prescribing rights and responsibility.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard supports rule-based medication surveillance; this is an existing capability whose runtime is not a new labour saving.
Model knowledge: native medication favourites can reuse fixed product fields without deciding clinical suitability or the patient's regimen.

assumptions: Boundary covers a medication prescription for the stated urological conditions, not dispensing or medicine administration. Shares are provisional, not measured.

The urologist obtains/validates clinical facts in s1, verifies medication list, risk factors and surveillance in s2, and chooses the medication. s3 captures actual dose, frequency, duration and advice manually; pharmacy identity is checked in s4. No automatic diagnosis or unpriced structured capture.

Test native favourites first. Only product/strength/route catalogue selection and fixed-field typing, 20% of s3, are removed. Individual regimen, corrections and ordinary ungated draft saving remain. Existing surveillance and electronic-send runtime earn no saving.

s4 checks the completed exact prescription and pharmacy destination before s5; edits void approval. s5 is the actual formal issue, fully retained at its small current interaction share. No model selects medicine or overrides alerts.
unknowns: Local authorisation and electronic issue workflow
research_questions: Can native favourites remove product typing while preserving full patient-specific dose and warning checks?

already_counted.description: Clinical decision, surveillance, regimen entry, exceptions and final checks remain.

incremental.description: Urologist reviews favourites after formulary or product changes.

approvals.approved_version: s4 final complete prescription, exact patient, product, regimen, warnings and pharmacy destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 20*0.20=4 fixed-entry hours removed less 1 upkeep gives 3 net. Cautious case: unusual fertility regimens require manual product/route selection, leaving 1.2 hours of supported catalogue reuse and 0.2 net; all clinical and final checks remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Choose current urology teaching content and prepare procedure demonstrations
Check teaching examples and demonstration safety against current practice
Teach clinical staff and supervise procedure practice

tasks.design: Keep content preparation, safe demonstration checking and clinical teaching human. Native {DOCS} materials are already available in this boundary; no new content-generation or staff-monitoring system is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clinical teaching must reflect current procedures and learner competence.
tasks.enabler_now: No established software change removes the substantive preparation or supervised practice.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe technique and explaining clinical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Adjust teaching and intervene during practice.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: clinical staff training combines substantive preparation, safety checks and supervised practice.

assumptions: Boundary is personally delivered training, not certification. Shares are provisional.
The urologist obtains staff needs and checks approved sources in s1; its actual preparation write is explicit. No new structured learner feed or transcript.
Test native content reuse first. Existing material is already reused here and no additional layout saving is established; all actual preparation and ordinary author saving remain.

No required completion record, credential activation or handout send is established in this teaching task. Add any actual first entry and separate final-version release with its own time; do not invent a trailing training log.
No proposed change means zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Which preparation or recording actions actually repeat beyond the current reusable clinical material?

already_counted.description: Preparation, safety checking and live teaching remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All focal work remains after separating preparation from teaching. An unfamiliar procedure still needs full preparation and supervision; no invented completion log supplies a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Limited documentation and native prescribing-field reuse reduce supporting work while clinical judgement, care direction and teaching stay with the urologist.
role.ambitious_version: No autonomous specialist advice, treatment decisions or expanded clinical authority are proposed.
